    • description

      public LogEncoder.Builder description(@Nullable String description)
      A human readable description of the formatter/pattern this encoder was built from (e.g. the actual pattern string), surfaced by LogReporter.Reportable instead of the built encoder only ever showing up as its bare concrete class name. Purely diagnostic: has no effect on encoding itself.
      Parameters:
      description - description, or null for none.
      Returns:
      this.

    • charset

      public LogEncoder.Builder charset(Charset charset)
      Charset to encode with. Only affects outputs whose LogEncoder.BufferHints.writeMethod() is LogOutput.WriteMethod.BYTES or LogOutput.WriteMethod.BYTE_BUFFER - the LogOutput.WriteMethod.STRING path hands a plain String to LogOutput.write(LogEvent, String), whose own default implementation is fixed to StandardCharsets.UTF_8 regardless of this setting, but no built-in output actually uses that write method. Defaults to StandardCharsets.UTF_8, or to contentType(ContentType)'s own charset if that was set and this was not. If both are set this charset is what is actually used to encode; contentType(ContentType) still controls what is reported to the output.
      Parameters:
      charset - charset to encode with.
      Returns:
      this.

    • contentType

      public LogEncoder.Builder contentType(LogOutput.ContentType contentType)
      Content type reported to the output. Use this when the formatter produces something other than plain text. Defaults to LogOutput.ContentType.StandardContentType.TEXT_PLAIN with whatever charset is in effect (see charset(Charset)).
      Parameters:
      contentType - content type reported to the output.
      Returns:
      this.

    • maxBufferSize

      public LogEncoder.Builder maxBufferSize(int maxBufferSize)
      Configures a maximum buffer size - see LogEncoder.Buffer.isOversized(). This is a soft ceiling, not a hard cap: a single event can still grow the buffer past this size while it is being encoded (nothing here truncates or rejects an oversized event), it just means the buffer's backing storage gets shrunk back down afterward instead of being kept at its grown size indefinitely - a quota that gets reclaimed after the fact, not enforced during the write. This, like charset, is a property of the encoder/buffer itself, not of whatever ends up reusing the buffer (e.g. an appender's ThreadLocal-cached one) - the buffer decides for itself, inside its own LogEncoder.Buffer.clear(), whether to shrink.
      Parameters:
      maxBufferSize - a negative value disables LogEncoder.Buffer.isOversized() entirely (the default).
      Returns:
      this.

    • initialBufferSize

      public LogEncoder.Builder initialBufferSize(int initialBufferSize)
      The capacity a fresh buffer is allocated with before any event has been encoded into it. Defaults to DirectByteBufferBuffer.DEFAULT_INITIAL_BYTE_CAPACITY.
      Parameters:
      initialBufferSize - initial buffer capacity, must be positive.
      Returns:
      this.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if not positive.

    • useGetBytes

      public LogEncoder.Builder useGetBytes(boolean useGetBytes)
      If set, converts to bytes with String.getBytes(Charset) on the fully formatted string instead of the default CharsetEncoder-based copy directly into a reused byte buffer. Only affects LogOutput.WriteMethod.BYTES/LogOutput.WriteMethod.BYTE_BUFFER outputs - always calls the byte[] overload directly regardless of which of those two hints an output actually declares.

      If never called, this resolves to true instead of the historical false default when LogProperties.GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY is enabled and the process is running as a GraalVM native image - see that property's javadoc for what it currently resolves to and why that is not a contract. Calling this method, either way, always wins over that.

      Parameters:
      useGetBytes - default is false, unless left unset and overridden by LogProperties.GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY.
      Returns:
      this.
